title: Dynamic Factor Analysis of Price Movements in the Philippine Stock Exchange
hypothesis: not stated: paper does not state a formal null hypothesis with numeric null value; model validation via correlation with PSEi and CAPM beta and significance at alpha=0.05 is descriptive, not a hypothesis test with test statistic and p-value printed.
data_sources: Phisix API via fastquant (PSE daily closing prices S_it)
Barrons market-data stocks for CAPM beta (footnote p.9)
Philippine quarterly GDP growth rates (source not stated beyond nowcasting application period 2015-2022)
sample: Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) daily stock prices and Philippine Stock Exchange Index (PSEi) composite returns. Historical stock price data via Python library fastquant wrapping Phisix API; PSEi data from https://stooq.com/q/d/?s=%5Epsei. Filter: drop stocks with more than 1% missing observations. Resulting analysis sample: 72 stocks (described as more than the top 30 in terms of market capitalization included in the PSEi). Percentage return R_it = (S_it - S_i(t-1))/S_i(t-1) where S_it is closing price of stock i at time t. GDP nowcasting uses Philippine quarterly GDP growth rates.
period_end: December 31, 2020; nowcasting out-of-sample period to December 31, 2022
method: 1. Obtain daily closing prices S_it for PSE stocks 2015-01-01 to 2020-12-31 via fastquant/Phisix and PSEi index same period via stooq.com.
2. Apply sample filter: parameter threshold 1%: drop any stock with >1% missing observations.

4. Determine number of common factors n using Bai-Ng information criteria IC1, IC2, IC3 as in Eq.2-4: ln V(n) + penalty where V(n) is mean of squared residuals when n common factors estimated via PCA. Evaluate n=0 (white noise) vs n=1,2. Select n=1 as best, n=2 as viable alternative.
5. Determine lag orders p (VAR for F_t) and q (AR for Z_it) via Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC): DFM(n=1,p=3,q=5) and DFM(n=2,p=2,q=5).

6. Formulate DFM as linear Gaussian state-space: Y_t = M X_t + eps_t, X_t = T X_{t-1} + eta_t with Sigma_eps=0 and Sigma_eta=diag(I_n,0,...,0, sigma^2,0,...,0). Estimate parameters M,T,Sigma by maximum likelihood using Kalman filter prediction/update and Rauch-Tung-Striebel smoother: mu_{t|t-1}=T mu_{t-1|t-1}, Sigma_{t|t-1}=T Sigma_{t-1|t-1} T'+Sigma_eta; K_t=Sigma_{t|t-1}M'(M Sigma_{t|t-1}M'+Sigma_eps)^{-1}; mu_{t|t}=mu_{t|t-1}+K_t(Y_t-M mu_{t|t-1}); Sigma_{t|t}=Sigma_{t|t-1}-K_t M Sigma_{t|t-1}; J_t=Sigma_{t|t}T' Sigma_{t+1|t}^{-1}; mu_{t|t'}=mu_{t|t}+J_t(mu_{t+1|t'}-mu_{t+1|t}).

7. Extract Kalman-smoothed common factors F_t (n=1) and F_t=[F1t,F2t]' (n=2) and idiosyncratic factors Z_it, and loadings beta_i, sigma_i. Estimate VAR coefficients Lambda_j and AR coefficients Psi_j.

8. Validation: compute Pearson correlations between (Kalman-smoothed) F_t and PSEi returns, between F_t and principal components, and between loadings beta_i and CAPM beta. Test significance of Lambda, beta_i, sigma_i at alpha=0.05 (ns = not significant).

9. GDP nowcasting: in-sample training January 1, 2015 to December 31, 2020; out-of-sample evaluation January 1, 2021 to December 31, 2022. Benchmark AR(1) for quarterly GDP growth. Augmented model: transform daily F_t into monthly indicators per calendar month (mean and standard deviation of F1t and F2t) to match quarterly frequency; to avoid leakage use Kalman-smoothed F_t in-sample and Kalman-filtered F_t out-of-sample; regress GDP growth on AR(1) plus monthly indicators via OLS. Evaluate via RMSE in-sample and out-of-sample.
